  • spline_vf : Spline

static classify_fixed_point(J: ndarray, eps: float = 0.0001) → str[source]

Classify a fixed point using linear stability analysis of its Jacobian.

The classification is determined from the eigenvalue spectrum of the Jacobian matrix evaluated at the fixed point.

Parameters:

  • J (ndarray of shape (d, d)) – Jacobian matrix of the vector field at the fixed point.

  • eps (float, default=1e-4) – Numerical tolerance used to determine whether eigenvalues are considered zero or have non-negligible imaginary parts.

Returns:

One of:

  • ”Stable node (sink)”

  • ”Unstable node (source)”

  • ”Saddle”

  • ”Degenerate”

  • ”Center”

  • ”Spiral in”

  • ”Spiral out”

  • ”Mixed focus”

Return type:

str

Notes

Let \(\lambda_i \in \mathbb{C}\) denote the eigenvalues of J.

  • Stability is determined by the sign of \(\Re(\lambda_i)\).

  • Purely real spectra correspond to node or saddle behavior.

  • Complex conjugate pairs indicate rotational (spiral or center) dynamics.

  • A fixed point is:

    • Stable if all \(\Re(\lambda_i) < 0\)

    • Unstable if all \(\Re(\lambda_i) > 0\)

    • A saddle if signs are mixed

This classification corresponds to the local linearization of the dynamical system near the fixed point.

identify_fixed_points(Xg: ndarray, Vg: ndarray, *, grid_shape: tuple, speed_smooth_sigma: float = 1.0, global_speed_quantile: float = 0.1, radius_percent: float = 0.2, weighted: bool = True) → List[Dict][source]

Identify and classify fixed points from grid-sampled velocities.

Parameters:

  • Xg (ndarray (Ng, d)) – Grid coordinates.

  • Vg (ndarray (Ng, d)) – Velocity evaluated on grid.

  • grid_shape (tuple) – Shape of grid used for reshaping.

  • speed_smooth_sigma (float) – Gaussian smoothing bandwidth.

  • global_speed_quantile (float) – Global speed threshold for filtering.

  • radius_percent (float) – Neighborhood radius relative to embedding scale.

  • weighted (bool) – Whether to use weighted Jacobian fitting.

Returns:

Each dict contains:

  • position : ndarray (d,)

  • jacobian : ndarray (d, d)

  • type : str

Return type:

list of dict

flowmap.geometry.gradient_analyzer module

class flowmap.geometry.gradient_analyzer.GeneGradientAnalyzer(emb)[source]

Bases: object

Analyze gene-level gradients in embedding space.

This class evaluates the geometry of gene-expression gradients reconstructed via the gene-level spline.

For each cell, the spline Jacobian provides:

J(z) = ∂X_gene / ∂z

Combined with the pullback metric, this allows computing:

  • Riemannian gradients

  • Alignment with local velocity

  • Parallel / orthogonal components

No plotting is performed here. Visualization should be handled in the plotting module.

compute_relative_gradients(neighbor_indices: ndarray, gene_indices: ndarray, weight: str = 'magnitude') → Dict[str, ndarray][source]

Compute relative orientation of gene gradients to velocity.

Parameters:

  • neighbor_indices (ndarray) – Cells near region of interest.

  • gene_indices (ndarray) – Genes to analyze.

  • weight ({"magnitude", "uniform"}, default="magnitude") – Weighting scheme for averaging across cells.

Returns:

Contains:

  • anglesndarray

    Mean angle (radians) relative to velocity direction.

  • magnitudesndarray

    Mean projected gradient magnitude.

Return type:

dict

class flowmap.geometry.LagrangianPathOptimizer(embedding, D: float = 1.0, lam: float = 0.0)[source]

Bases: object

Minimum-action path computation for FlowMap embeddings.

This class computes transition trajectories under the action:

\[S[x] = \frac{1}{2D} \int ||\dot{x} - v(x)||^2 dt + \lambda \int ||\dot{x}||^2 dt\]

where:

  • v(x) is the embedded vector field

  • D is the diffusion constant

  • λ is an arc-length regularization weight

The optimizer:

  1. Initializes a path via Dijkstra on a kNN graph

  2. Refines the path by gradient descent on the action functional

fit_path(start: ndarray, end: ndarray, *, distance_mode: str = 'embed', subsample_n: int = 4000, k: int = 20, alpha: float = 0.0, n_segments: int = 100, lr: float = 0.005, iters: int = 300) → Dict[source]

Compute minimum-action transition path between two states.

Parameters:

  • start (ndarray (d,)) – Starting coordinate.

  • end (ndarray (d,)) – Ending coordinate.

  • distance_mode ({"embed", "orig"}) – Graph geometry for initialization.

  • subsample_n (int) – Number of points used for graph.

  • k (int) – Number of nearest neighbors.

  • alpha (float) – Velocity-alignment weight.

  • n_segments (int) – Number of discretization segments.

  • lr (float) – Gradient descent learning rate.

  • iters (int) – Number of refinement iterations.

Returns:

  • path_init

  • path_refined

  • dt

Return type:

dict with keys
